items.title: SpaceX Crew-12 docks at ISS after medical evacuation cut short previous mission

featured_image.name: NASA's SpaceX Crew-12 Secured in Spacecraft

items.description:
Four astronauts aboard NASA's SpaceX Crew-12 mission docked at the International Space Station on Saturday, bringing the orbital laboratory back to its full seven-person complement following an unprecedented medical evacuation that cut short the previous crew's stay.

The Dragon spacecraft Freedom linked up with the station's Harmony module at approximately 3:15 p.m. EST, capping a 34-hour journey that began with a predawn launch from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station on Friday. The mission marks NASA's twelfth operational crew rotation under its Commercial Crew Program with SpaceX.[1][2]

items.title: UK and allies say Navalny was killed with rare dart frog toxin

featured_image.name: UK, allies say they're convinced Kremlin critic Navalny was poisoned

items.description:
Russian opposition leader Alexei Navalny was poisoned with epibatidine, a lethal toxin found in South American poison dart frogs, according to a joint announcement by five European nations on the second anniversary of his death in a Siberian penal colony.

The United Kingdom, France, Germany, Sweden, and the Netherlands issued a joint statement on Saturday confirming that analyses of samples from Navalny "conclusively confirmed the presence of epibatidine," a substance not found naturally in Russia. The announcement, made at the Munich Security Conference, directly implicates the Russian government in Navalny's death, with the coalition stating that "only the Russian state had the combined means, motive and disregard for international law" to carry out the attack.[1][2][3]

items.title: Rubio urges transatlantic unity as Europe stresses self-reliance

featured_image.name: In Munich, Rubio urges transatlantic unity but lashes Europe on migration

items.description:
The 62nd Munich Security Conference opened this weekend to a fractured Western alliance, with European leaders delivering pointed assessments of transatlantic relations while U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio attempted to reassure anxious allies that Washington still values its oldest partnerships.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz set the tone on Friday when he declared that the rules-based world order "no longer exists" and acknowledged that "a deep divide has opened between Europe and the United States." Speaking directly to the American delegation, Merz warned that U.S. claims to global leadership have been "challenged, and possibly lost," while urging Europe to stop denying the scale of the geopolitical challenge it faces.[1][2]

items.title: Iran arrests over 50,000 in dragnet after deadly protest crackdown

featured_image.name: Arrests of protestors continue to roil Iran weeks after ...

items.description:
Iranian security forces have arrested more than 50,000 people in a sweeping campaign following a brutal crackdown last month that killed thousands of demonstrators, according to human rights groups. The dragnet, spanning major cities and rural towns, has targeted protesters, doctors, lawyers, students, actors, and reformist political figures, with many held incommunicado for days or weeks.[1][2]

The Associated Press reported that security agents have conducted late-night raids on homes and workplaces across the country, using surveillance footage and facial recognition technology to track down individuals who participated in protests that peaked in early January.[2][3]

items.title: NASA reviews Artemis II test data as moon mission eyes March

featured_image.name: More trouble for Artemis-II rocket, Moon launch likely delayed again

items.description:
NASA engineers are analyzing data from a confidence test conducted on February 12 as the agency works toward returning humans to the Moon for the first time in more than five decades. The test was designed to evaluate repairs made following a hydrogen leak that forced NASA to push back the Artemis II launch from its original February window.

During the test at Kennedy Space Center, operators partially filled the Space Launch System core stage liquid hydrogen tank to assess newly replaced seals in the propellant fueling area, NASA said in a statement. Teams encountered an issue with ground support equipment that reduced the flow of liquid hydrogen into the rocket, though engineers were able to achieve several key objectives and collect data at the same point in testing where a leak had been detected during the previous wet dress rehearsal.[1][2]

items.title: SpaceX Crew-12 to dock with ISS on Valentine's Day

featured_image.name: NASA and SpaceX set to launch Crew-12 to the ISS on Feb 13 ...

items.description:
A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket lifted off early Friday morning carrying four astronauts toward the International Space Station, marking the 12th operational crew rotation mission under NASA's Commercial Crew Program. The Crew Dragon capsule "Freedom" is set to dock with the orbiting outpost this afternoon, delivering a relief crew after an unprecedented medical evacuation last month left the station short-staffed.

The mission launched at 5:15 a.m. EST on February 13 from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida. The crew consists of NASA astronauts Jessica Meir, serving as commander, and Jack Hathaway as pilot, along with mission specialists Sophie Adenot of the European Space Agency and Andrey Fedyaev of Roscosmos.[1][2][3]

items.title: NASA extracts oxygen from lunar soil using solar energy

featured_image.name: Sunlight extracts oxygen from regolith using solar chemistry

items.description:
NASA has achieved a milestone in lunar resource utilization, completing integrated prototype testing that used concentrated solar energy to extract oxygen from simulated lunar soil. The Carbothermal Reduction Demonstration project, known as CaRD, confirmed the production of carbon monoxide through a solar-driven chemical reaction, marking a key advance toward sustaining human exploration on the Moon.[1][2]

The successful test represents a step toward enabling astronauts to produce propellant using only lunar materials and sunlight, which could reduce the cost and complexity of maintaining a long-term presence on the lunar surface. The same technology could eventually be adapted to convert carbon dioxide into oxygen and methane on Mars.[2][3]

items.title: Cornell study pinpoints global crop emissions to 10-kilometer resolution

featured_image.name: What's the Climate Cost of Growing Crops? - World Resources Institute

items.description:
Researchers have produced the most comprehensive map of global cropland greenhouse gas emissions to date, revealing that just four crops—rice, maize, oil palm, and wheat—account for nearly three-quarters of all emissions from farming, with rice alone responsible for 43%.

The study, published February 13 in Nature Climate Change, synthesizes data from ground measurements, remote sensing, inventory surveys, and hydrological models to achieve a spatial resolution of approximately 10 kilometers—enabling emissions to be pinpointed not just by country, but by individual crops and management practices.[1][2]

items.title: Blue Origin reveals accelerated Moon plan as SpaceX pivots from Mars

featured_image.name: Why Did Jeff Bezos Post a Turtle Image on X? And Why Is Elon ...

items.description:
The race to return humans to the lunar surface has entered a new phase this week, with both SpaceX and Blue Origin unveiling aggressive strategies to beat China to the Moon, while Beijing continues to make steady progress toward its 2030 landing goal.

On February 9, Elon Musk announced a dramatic shift in SpaceX's priorities, revealing that the company has pivoted toward building a "self-growing city" on the Moon within the next decade. The announcement, made on his social media platform X, marks a stark reversal for the billionaire, who as recently as last year dismissed lunar missions as a "distraction" from his Mars ambitions. According to Reuters, Musk said traveling to Mars is only possible every 26 months, while launches to the Moon can occur every 10 days, allowing SpaceX to "iterate much faster."[1][2][3]

items.title: Zelensky says Ukraine won't hold referendum on 'bad' peace deal

featured_image.name: Zelensky gives major update on potential Ukraine peace deal ...

items.description:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky offered a detailed account of his approach to peace negotiations with Russia in an exclusive interview with The Atlantic, published Thursday as he prepared to attend the Munich Security Conference. Speaking with journalist Simon Shuster, Zelensky emphasized Ukraine's willingness to engage constructively with U.S.-led proposals while setting firm conditions for any final agreement.

"The tactic we chose is for the Americans not to think that we want to continue the war," Zelensky told The Atlantic. "That's why we started supporting their proposals in any format that speeds things along."[1][2]
